title: dira ledger entry
description: A single entry in a dira ledger. Serialized as YAML frontmatter at the top of .dira/entries/<id>.md; the markdown body following the frontmatter is the entry's prose (the 'because'). One entry per file — see dec-0002 for why this is not JSONL.

id.description: Stable, immutable, ledger-local identifier. Never reused, never renumbered. Prefix encodes kind.

kind.description: The closed entry set. Deliberately closed: adding a sixth kind is how dira becomes Obsidian. Requires superseding cst-0002 to extend.

title.description: One line, imperative or declarative, no trailing period. This is what renders in the brief, so it must be legible with zero context.

state.description: Lifecycle state. Valid values depend on kind — see the allOf constraints below. Note that NO state here describes execution progress: planned/in-progress/completed/blocked are DERIVED by joining kazi, never stored (dec-0005).

created.description: RFC3339 UTC. Set once at capture, never rewritten.

updated.description: RFC3339 UTC. Bumped on any field change. Absent means never modified since creation.

edges.description: Typed, directed relationships. Edges are stored on the SUBJECT entry, so a single file write is a complete mutation — no two-file transactions, therefore no partial commits.

alternatives.description: For decisions: the roads not taken, each with its own reason. This is the field that makes `dira why` worth reading and `dira check` possible — a decision without alternatives is an assertion, not a decision.

tags.description: Freeform retrieval aids. Not a taxonomy — do not build features that depend on specific tag values.

source.description: Provenance: how this entry came to exist. Present on agent-captured entries so a human can always audit what a hook inferred versus what a human confirmed.

confirmed_by.description: Who dispositioned this entry. 'human' means a person confirmed it; an agent identifier means it was auto-logged provisionally and is still staged. Absent on entries that need no disposition (notes).

adr.description: Relative path to the mirrored ADR file, when adr_mirror is enabled for this ledger. The ADR is exhaust, not truth — this entry is the record. Deleting the ADR must never lose information.

private.description: Marks an entry as never-exportable. Enforced at read time by the inheritance rule (cst-0003): a private entry may be injected into a local session brief but must never be written into, or quoted into, a downstream public ledger.

then.description: Intents are directions, not tasks. They are achieved or abandoned — never 'done', because doneness belongs to kazi.

A decision MUST record at least the alternative of not doing it — unless it is still staged, in which case nobody has decided anything yet. Rejected decisions are first-class and permanent: they are the substrate `dira check` reads to stop relitigation.

A staged decision is a regex-tier proposal awaiting a human (dec-0003). `alternatives` is not required and may be empty, because the tier that captured it cannot know what was rejected or why, and a why_not it invented would be quoted back at the user three weeks later as their own reasoning. Tier 2 and the disposition flow fill this in; until then its absence is the honest record.

else.description: Once a decision leaves `staged`, a human has stood behind it and the roads not taken are part of what they stood behind. `alternatives: []` satisfied the letter of the old rule while asserting that there were none — which is exactly the assertion this field exists to prevent.

then.description: An open question with a `blocks` edge is a decision-blocker — the class of blockage kazi structurally cannot see, because it exists upstream of any goal.
Constraints inherit downward through derives_from and are evaluated by every `dira check` in every descendant ledger.
Notes are the escape hatch for thoughts that are not yet any of the other four. They surface once in the next brief and then decay — a note that matters becomes an intent, a decision, or a question.

ref.description: A reference to an entry, optionally namespaced by ledger. Bare form (dec-0060) resolves within the current ledger; namespaced form (sire:int-0002) resolves via the ledger map in .dira/config.toml. Namespacing is what makes the tiers fractal without a server.

type.description: supersedes: this entry replaces an earlier one, which flips to superseded. derives_from: this entry serves a parent intent, possibly in a parent ledger — absence of this edge on an active intent is what the orphan-work drift flag detects. informs: weaker context link, no lifecycle effect. blocks: this entry gates another; the source is typically an open question. realized_by: this decision is carried out by an external execution artifact, the only edge type whose target is not a dira ref.

to.description: Target. A dira ref for all edge types except realized_by, which takes an external URI (kazi:<proposal-or-goal-id>). Kept as a single string rather than a union so the whole edge set is greppable with one pattern.

note.description: Optional one line on why this edge exists. Renders in `dira why` chains.

option.description: The road not taken, stated as though it had been chosen.

why_not.description: The actual reason. This string is what gets quoted back at you three weeks later when you try to relitigate, so it must survive loss of context.

revisit_if.description: The condition that would legitimately reopen this. Distinguishes a closed door from a locked one, and gives `dira check` something better to say than 'no'.
examples: cold-start latency stops being the binding constraint

hook.description: Which capture point produced this entry.

session.description: Opaque session identifier, for tracing an entry back to the conversation that produced it.

excerpt.description: The transcript fragment the capture was inferred from. Bounded — this is evidence for review, not a transcript archive.

tier.description: How the entry was extracted. regex: `dira sniff`, cheap and lossy, always staged. semantic: the already-running Claude session filled it in via the skill. human: typed by a person. dira never embeds a model client, so there is no 'api' tier (dec-0003).
